passage:
During a heat wave, the city opened cooling centers in libraries and community halls. People without air conditioning could rest there, drink water, and avoid dangerous heat.
Volunteers helped older residents find transportation. Posters were placed in several languages.
A student volunteering at one center saw that heat did not affect everyone equally. People with money could cool their homes. Others depended on public spaces.
The heat wave became a lesson in fairness.
Weather may fall on a whole city, but people do not face it with the same protection. Public planning matters most when private comfort is not enough.
